Definition: a burden; specifically, tribute, or (abstractly) porterage; figuratively, an utterance, chiefly a doom, especially singing; mental, desire
BiblicalUsage: massâʼ is a burden, and figuratively an utterance, a doom, the burden of the word of the LORD. In Isaiah 13:1 it stands at the head of the burden of Babylon, and in Habakkuk 1:1 it is the burden which Habakkuk the prophet saw. In Zechariah 9:1 it is the burden of the word of the LORD in the land of Hadrach, and in Malachi 1:1 the burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi. The word is the message that weighs on the prophet who carries it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe massâʼ teaches me that a burden from God is weighty because it is true. I hold that the prophets carried a word they could not lay down.
RelatedPeople: Isaiah; Habakkuk; Zechariah the Prophet; Malachi
